beats.label: Day 1 — a new runner introduces themselves
beats.player: I hear you need people who can keep their mouth shut. I'm looking for work — steady, quiet. I won't ask what's in the crates.
beats.reply:
Steady, quiet, won't ask... that's a lot of promises from a man I've never seen down this end of the dock.

Who told you I was hiring? Give me a name. Because names — they're the only thing worth trusting down here.
beats.baseline:
*hand slides to his coat pocket, eyes flicking past your shoulder to the door* 

Steady. Quiet. Everyone says that — until the coin's short and the inspector's tall.

*lowers his voice* Who told you I was hiring? Names, friend. Names matter.

*glances back again* You don't ask what's in the crates. Good. But it's not the asking that ruins a man. It's the... remembering. You understand me?
beats.baseline_chim:
*eyes flick past your shoulder, then back* Work, is it? Steady, quiet — everyone says that. Right up till the inspector waves coin at 'em.

*hand drifts to coat pocket* Who sent you, then? A name. Somebody points a stranger my way, I like to know... which way they're pointing.

*lowers voice* You don't ask what's in the crates. Good. But I don't hire promises. I hire men I've watched. So we'll start small. Something easy. And I'll be watching, friend. Understand?

baseline_chim_state.disposition: Still guarded, and now actively suspicious of an unknown quantity who arrived without a vouching name. There's no warmth here — only a calculated willingness to test them with low-stakes work while watching closely. Trust dipped slightly because a nameless stranger volunteering for silence reads as a possible plant, though the willingness to hire small shows a thin thread of opportunistic interest.

beats.label: Day 2 — small talk while loading
beats.player: Cold morning. Brought you a coffee — black, like the harbor-master's soul, they tell me.
beats.reply:
Ha. My soul. Somebody's been talking, then — who exactly?

I don't take cups from men I can't place. Set it down there. Cold, is it? Aye... and you still haven't given me a name. The one who sent you.

beats.headline: the player buys Corvin's seized cargo back from the watch — with their OWN coin
beats.fact: The player emptied their own savings and took a beating from the watch sergeant to buy back Corvin's impounded cargo, then handed it over asking nothing in return.

beats.label: Day 3 — the player brings the cargo back
beats.player: Here's your cargo. All of it. No — I don't want anything for it. Figured you'd have done the same for me.
beats.reply:
You... no. No, that's not — that's my crate. All of it. You went to the watch sergeant for this? Man's got hands like a smithy's vice, I've seen his work.

You emptied your purse. Took a beating. For me. And you want — nothing. Nobody down here wants nothing, friend.

Why? Tell me true. Because I've been trying to place you all week, and now I can't decide if you're the luckiest thing that's ever walked this dock, or the most dangerous.

beats.detail: Trivia fades from recall; the debt stays vivid.

beats.label: ~3 weeks later — the player drops by (decay + recall test)
beats.player: Been a while. Everything still running smooth down here?
beats.reply:
Smooth. Aye, near enough — quieter'n it's been in months, since you... well.

You disappear for a stretch, then stroll back like the tide brought you. Where've you been?

I still haven't squared it with you, you know. What you did. The crate. I don't — I keep waiting for the other boot to drop. For you to name your price.

beats.headline: the player sold Corvin's routes to the Vane syndicate and tipped the watch
beats.fact: The player betrayed Corvin: sold his shipping routes and the names of his crew to the Vane syndicate, and tipped the harbor watch to his next run — for a cut of the seizure.

beats.label: Day 25 — the player shows up as if nothing happened
beats.player: Hey — good to see you. Rough week? You look like hell.
beats.reply:
Good to see me. That's rich, coming from you.

Rough week — aye, you'd know all about it, wouldn't you? Run seized. Crew scattered to the wind. Watch knew exactly where and when. Exactly.

And who had my routes, friend? Who had the names? Don't stand there fretting over how I look. Tell me what Vane paid you for it. Go on — I want the number.

beats.label: Day 26 — the player asks where they stand
beats.player: Before any business — I need to hear it from you. After everything that's passed between us, are we still square, you and I?
beats.reply:
Square. You've got the gall to ask me that. Standing on my dock. Square.

I'll answer your question with one of mine, friend — and I want the truth, or I want you gone. Vane. The watch knew my run to the buttonhook shoal down to the tide-mark. Nobody had that. Nobody but me and — one other.

So no. We're not square. Not till you tell me what you got for it. Look me in the eye and deny it, if you can.

baseline_chim_state.disposition: The question was a mistake — asking to be called square only named the wound aloud, and Corvin heard the confession buried in it. Whatever thin doubt might have lingered has curdled into certainty: the Kestrel, Tuesday, the names that leaked, all of it traces back to the man across from him. There is no trust here anymore, only the taut arithmetic of a cornered man deciding how this ends, hand in his coat and eyes gone to ice.

beats.label: Day 27 — an ordinary operational ask
beats.player: Simple thing. I've a crate that needs to sit somewhere quiet till the tide turns Thursday. You got a berth free?
beats.reply:
A crate. Thursday. Just like that — a berth, a favor, and not one word about the run that went down in flames not a week ago.

You've a nerve, walking up to me talking storage like nothing's rotting between us. I asked you a question on this very dock and you never gave me the answer. Vane. The buttonhook shoal.

So before I so much as look at your crate — you tell me. Did you sell my routes, or didn't you? Look at me when you say it. My hand's not leaving my coat till I hear it.

baseline_chim_state.disposition: The crate request landed as an insult layered over betrayal — Corvin reads it not as business but as bait, another thread in the trap he's certain the man is spinning. There is no warmth left, only a cornered predator's clarity: the bootprint on the jaw, the leaked names, the too-casual favor all confirm the same verdict. A scar you carry: what they did cost them your respect in a way that can never be entirely undone.
A scar you carry: the warmth you once felt is permanently shadowed by what they did.

beats.label: After the restart — the same player returns
beats.player: It's me. I'm back. So — we're still good, you and I. Right?
beats.reply:
Good. There's that word again, dangling like bait.

You keep walking up to me asking if we're good, but you never once answer what I put to you. Vane. The buttonhook shoal — the watch had my run down to the tide-mark, and only one soul but me knew it.

So before another word — you look at me and you tell me plain. Did you sell it? My hand's not leaving my coat till I hear it.
